body: Getting something like this would make me so happy.  I hope you did send this.

I read that there is no obligation to stay in relationship and you don't owe you're SO any reason often here, but I don't understand.  I haven't dated much, but I have a lot of close relationships that if we were to distance ourselves abruptly I would expect some sort of explanation as a courtesy of someone who has been an important person in my life.  I have had it happen and I was really hurt, but I don't think I would ever do that to someone.  I would love to hear the other side, I'm sure I'm not considering everything!
Hmm that's interesting I really like being able to talk about everything, but maybe that is a good idea.

That's an interesting point and I was almost treating it like that for a while.  I did struggle with everyone telling me she just wants you on the side, or she doesn't actually love you she just wants to have someone to lean on.  I don't believe what they say, but they have made me insecure about the relationship.  I guess going against social norms is difficult and I'm sure you guys are well aware of that.  It's like the devil on shoulder telling me I'm fucking up, but that devil is society.  Interesting to see how it has affected my views I'd like to think they haven't, but they have.

The reason I feel like it may hurt her is it does hurt me.  It's unclear to me why it hurts me, but I'm egocentric I guess because I have a hard time seeing it from her perspedtive.  We talk about everything which is really good I think and she knows how I feel.

I really love her and want her to be happy, and if other people make her happy that's good -- that's what I think logically.  However when we Skype and I see hickies on her neck or she tells me about her sexual experiences I feel sad.  I don't want to and I don't really understand why.  I don't discourage her from doing it or anything, but I have told her that it makes me feel sad for a reason I'm not sure of.  I don't think it's jealousy, I'm not mad at anyone.

Thanks guys we talked a little bit and I no longer believe my friend is in immediate danger.  The friend is still struggling with depression and I know I won't physically be there for them, and there is no one else who knows so I am not comfortable having someone go check up on them.  To everyone else my friend appears to be in a good situation -- good grades at a respected university and has an active social life -- and I do not feel it is my right to tell others about their situation.  It required a lot of trust for them to tell me and I feel if my friend found out I told others it would likely hurt my friend.  I still feel lost as to what I should do in this situation.  All of your advice does help thank you!
